chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja' ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad' ibn al-Husayn' ibn Abi al-Khattab' from Muhammad' ibn Isma'il' from Salih' ibn 'Uqbah' from Bashir' al-Dahhan' who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Any believer who visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, on a day other than an Eid or 'Arafah, Allah will record for him twenty Hajj (pilgrimages) and twenty 'Umrah (minor pilgrimages), purified and accepted, and twenty battles (of jihad) with a Messenger Prophet or a Just Imam.

key_terms.زَارَ: visited (specifically referring to Ziyarah of the Imams)
key_terms.عَارِفاً بِحَقِّهِ: knowing his right (acknowledging the spiritual status and due rights of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husayn on a day other than Eid or 'Arafah?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this hadith to emphasize the unique merit of visiting Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) outside the major communal festivals, highlighting individual devotion. The reward of twenty accepted pilgrimages and battles with Prophets underscores the high spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia theology, linking physical visitation to the culmination of faith and martyrdom.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: Muḥammad ibn Ja’far narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Allāh will register twenty purified and accepted Hajj and ‘Umrah and the reward of (fighting in) twenty battles with one of Allāh’s messengers or with a Just Imam for any believer who goes to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) knowing his rights on any day other than an Eid and the Day of ‘Arafah. The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.).
